sentences.text:
Author: Surepalli Nanda
Bench: Surepalli Nanda
 Hon'Ble Mrs Justice Surepalli Nanda
 Writ Petition No.17774 of 2023
Order:

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Irrigation and Command Area Development appearing for respondent No.1, learned Government Pleader for Finance and Planning Department appearing for respondent No.2 and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.3 and 4.
2.

The grievance of the petitioners in this writ petition is that in spite of Competent Civil Court passing a judgment and decree, dated 04.12.2012 in L.A.O.P.No.24 of 2011 and the petitioners filing E.P.No.7 of 2023 on the file of Court of Senior Civil Judge, Narayanpet, the judgement debtor i.e..,
respondent No.4 failed to deposit the decretal amount even after lapse of more than eleven years and the said E.P is being adjourned from time to time.
3.

The facts of the case are that the land in Survey No.169/A/AA situated at Makthal Village and Mandal, WP_17774_2023 SN,J Mahabubnagar District, was acquired by Land Acquisition officer,
by passing an Award, dated 18.11.2010 and on the request made by the petitioners herein, the same was referred to the Court of Senior Civil Judge, Narayanpet under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act, 1894').
Considering the said reference, the Civil Court passed a judgment and decree, dated 04.12.2012, enhancing the compensation and the same was modified in LAAS No.363 of 2013.

Seeking execution of the said judgment and decree as modified,
the petitioners herein filed E.P.No.7 of 2023 on the file of Court of Senior Civil Judge, Narayanpet.
In the said E.P., respondent No.4 herein stated to have entered appearance and the said execution proceedings are being dragged on from time to time and are still pending.
Respondent No.4 herein failed to deposit the decretal amount in spite of the said judgment and decree having become final.

Aggrieved by the said inaction on the part of respondent No.4 and the action of respondent Nos.1 and 2 in making available the required funds for complying with the said judgment and decree, the present writ petition is filed.

WP_17774_2023 SN,J 4. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition brings on record the written instructions vide Lr.No.F/32/2021, dated 10.07.2023 and in particular relevant portion of said written instructions reads as under:

sentences.text: "In this regard this Office submitted the Decretal charges proposals for an amount of Rs.28,04,304/- (In words Rupees Twenty Eight lakhs four thousand three hundred and four only) to the District Collector, Narayanpet.

The District Collector,
Narayanpet recommended to the Chief Commissioner, Land Administration,
Hyderabad.
The Chief Commissioner, Land Administration, Hyderabad recommended to the Spl. Chief Secretary Govt. I & CAD (LA) Department vide Lr.No.CCLA-LA-1/LAS1/23/2023-LA-1 dated 01.06.2023.
At present the file is under process in Principle Secretary Irrigation Secretariat, Hyderabad Telangana for issue G.O Rt and Sanction of Budget.
Soon after received the amount the same is deposit in Civil Court, Narayanpet for compliance court orders."

5. Having, taken note of the facts and circumstances of the case, especially, the fact that the property of the petitioners was acquired, as early as, in the year 2008 and they are deprived of their property without fixing the proper compensation and though proper compensation was fixed by the competent Civil Court on reference under Section 18 of WP_17774_2023 SN,J the Act, 1894, as early as on 04.12.2012, the petitioners are not being paid with said compensation as of date i.e., even after lapse of more than eleven years, and in the light of law laid down by this Court in the case of Bhamidipati Annaporna Bhavani v. Land Acquisition Officer1 holding that the writ petition is maintainable even when execution proceedings are pending seeking a direction for payment of compensation as fixed by the reference Court, this Court is left with no other option except to declare that the action on the part of the respondents is totally arbitrary, illegal and violative of Article 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India.
6.
